carousel.short: I understand the bureaucracy. Explaining myself is harder.
carousel.long: I understand the bureaucracy. Explaining myself is harder. So I built a bureaucrat for the bureaucracy.

carousel.short: A phone line, a voice, a knowledge base.
carousel.long: A phone line, a voice, a knowledge base. A messaging bot, a phone line, a multilingual voice and a knowledge base of every public entity and utility I deal with. It calls, answers, and sets up or cancels a service. Thanks to it, I didn't hire a personal assistant.

carousel.short: It knows when to hand over.
carousel.long: It knows when to hand over. When it's missing information, it brings me into the call instead of guessing, and that rule matters more than the voice.

carousel.short: Diagram: What it does, and what it never gets.
carousel.long: Diagram: What it does, and what it never gets. Everything it needs to make the call, a rule to hand it over, and the keys kept out on purpose.

Where I stop trusting myself. I'm an architect, not a programmer, so once the work on our platform became delicate, I added tests, reviews and a few hours a month of an experienced engineer. The engineer knows what questions to ask. I don't know them yet.

carousel.short: Start from friction you actually have, and write down what the agent may never touch before it…
carousel.long: Start from friction you actually have, and write down what the agent may never touch before it touches anything. Building one yourself? Tell me what it will never touch.

quote.short: Quote card: "AI lets you build for your own problem faster than ever, but it won't tell you what…
quote.long: Quote card: "AI lets you build for your own problem faster than ever, but it won't tell you what to withhold or where your judgment ends." Asaf Eyzenkot, Suf Zen, founder of Realization.

cover.long: A bureaucrat for the bureaucracy. Asaf Eyzenkot, Suf Zen, founder of Realization.
